item.description:
No dot for a Codex turn that never happened

Wortel 2026.46.1 · 2026-11-09

Idle Codex sessions stay quiet. After a while, every Codex session in the sidebar could get a dot and a notification at the same moment, though none of them had done anything. Codex writes a short recap under a conversation once it has been in the background for half an hour, and to Wortel that looked like a short turn. Codex also spins its title while it starts up, which looked the same. Claude Code sessions were fixed for this in 2026.44.4. Codex sessions now get the same check: a real turn is always written to the conversation Codex keeps on disk, so when nothing was written, Wortel raises no dot.

One session can run the others

Wortel 2026.45.1 · 2026-11-03

wortel reaches every session, not just its own. wortel list shows your sessions and what each is doing. wortel read <session> prints what’s on its screen, and --lines 50 takes the last 50 lines. wortel send <session> "text" --enter types into it the way a paste would, so a prompt of several lines arrives as one. wortel wait <session> waits until the agent in it has finished its turn, until some text appears (--for READY) or until it exits, and exits with 124 if the time runs out. A session can be named by its id or its name, and wortel new already prints the new session’s id, so one agent can start another, give it a task, wait for it and read the answer.

Your prompt history on ⌘Y. Everything you’ve typed to Claude Code, Codex and Pi, from any session and any project, with this project’s prompts first. Pick one and it goes into the session’s input without being sent. Wortel keeps none of it itself: it reads the history the agents already keep.

Select several sessions at once. ⌘-click adds a session, ⇧-click takes a range, and right-clicking the selection closes, pins, moves, marks or colours all of them. Esc goes back to one. And View ▸ Sort Unread First lifts the sessions that want you to the top of each section, without touching the order you dragged them into.

Notifications say what the agent answered. Instead of “Finished, your move”, a notification now starts with the agent’s answer, and a question shows the question.

Wortel notices when you’ve walked away. A session you had open in front used to count as seen, even if you’d left before the agent finished. After a minute with no keyboard or mouse, it now gets its dot and its notification like any other.

No stray characters after a relaunch. Reattaching a session replays what it printed while Wortel was closed, and the terminal used to answer the old questions in there again (where’s the cursor, what’s the background colour), which could land in an agent’s prompt as ^[[24;1R. Those answers are now dropped.

No dot for a turn that never happened

Wortel 2026.44.4 · 2026-10-30

Idle compaction no longer looks like a finished turn. Claude Code now compacts a long conversation by itself after it has sat idle for about 54 minutes, so the summary is written before its prompt cache expires. That runs for half a minute with the same spinner as a turn, so Wortel told you “Finished, your move” on a session where nothing had happened and nothing was waiting for you. Wortel now reads what Claude wrote down, sees a compaction, and leaves the session alone.

Idle sessions stay quiet after a relaunch. Right after a relaunch, anything that repainted an idle Claude session for a couple of seconds could pass for a short turn, and several sessions could light up in the same second. A real turn always writes to the conversation, so when Wortel is going by the screen alone it now checks there first, and raises no dot if nothing was written. A session is also no longer named from a turn that didn’t happen.

Change Directory no longer waits forever after a compaction. A move waiting for Claude to finish could take the compaction’s summary for a prompt still owed an answer, and never go ahead. It now looks past the summary.
